brief: J.P. Morgan's 2026 Global Macro Conference concluded equities and Treasury yields can rise together for now, because AI-driven capex and resilient earnings support stocks while deficits, heavier issuance and a rising term premium push long-end yields higher. Higher policy rates are transmitting less to the real economy since AI, healthcare and services are less rate-sensitive, so the yield level that would break equities has likely risen from 5% toward 5.5-6%. Fed hikes are now consensus, with 83% of surveyed investors expecting one before end-2026, and eight of nine tracked developed-market central banks are projected to hike this year as inflation stays above target, partly because AI capex is itself inflationary. AI capex is viewed as durable because financing is diversifying across bonds, private credit and structured deals, though permitting and execution, not demand, are becoming the binding constraint. Geopolitical and oil risk premia are seen as underpriced, with a 2027 Brent scenario spread between $64 in a baseline of peace and $87 under a forever-conflict scenario. Midterms are expected to produce a split Congress, with affordability politics the dominant driver regardless of outcome.
